label: David Papineau, The Rise of Physicalism…: The completeness of physics: every PHYSICAL_2 effect is…
locator: pp.3–12 p.8 (The Completeness of Physics and the Argument for Physicalism)
interpretation: Papineau's 'more precise version' of the completeness of physics: all physical effects are fully determined by law by prior physical occurrences (p.8; note 2 widens it to the chances of physical occurrences under quantum indeterminism). He asserts it, not only reports it: it is the crucial empirical premise of the causal argument (p.7), and the conclusion (pp.32-33, passage PAPINEAU-RISE-PHYSICALISM-13-33) says there is now good reason to believe that all physical effects are due to physical causes, a premise fully established by normal inductive standards though not certain. 'Physical' is his stipulated sense, specifiable without the special vocabulary at issue (pp.12-13), and causal relata are read as facts or property instantiations (p.10). The thesis is about physical effects only and does not assert physicalism (p.8). Not read here: physicalism itself (restricted at pp.11-12 to whatever interacts causally with the physical world), any claim about God, and any identification of his determining prior occurrences with the case's movers; that last step is the separate unattributed bridge STMT-PRIOR-PHYSICAL-DETERMINATION-GIVES-MOVER. Papineau does not respond to Aquinas; this is a research assessment of his own thesis.
